resources.string: InboxIQ
Texts, sorted on this phone

InboxIQ is a messaging app. It files each conversation as Personal, Work, Transaction, Promo, Code, Spam or Scam, using a small model that runs on your phone. To do that it has to be your default SMS app.
EXAMPLE ONLY: made-up messages, not yours
Codes get a Copy button. Likely scams are flagged. Your own texts are sorted the same way once you switch.

What changes when you switch
Android allows one default SMS app. InboxIQ would take over from %1$s: it receives and sends your texts, and its notifications replace that app\'s.
Android allows one default SMS app. InboxIQ would take over from your current one: it receives and sends your texts, and its notifications replace that app\'s.

InboxIQ handles SMS and picture messages (MMS) only. RCS chat features in Google Messages, such as typing indicators, read receipts and Wi-Fi chats, do not work while InboxIQ is the default, and chats that live only inside Google Messages may not appear here.
What stays

Your existing texts are copied into a private database on this phone. The originals stay in Android\'s message storage; nothing is deleted. Texts you send and receive while InboxIQ is the default are saved there too, so the app you switch back to has them. Your contacts and your old app are untouched.
Switching back

Open Android Settings, then Apps, Default apps, SMS app, and pick your old app (the wording varies by phone). In InboxIQ, Settings has a button that opens that screen. It is about three taps, and you can do it at any time.
What it will do
Receive and send SMS and picture messages. Look up names in your contacts if Android allows it. Use the microphone only while you hold the voice memo button.
What it will not do
Upload your messages to sort them. Show ads, use analytics or ask you to sign in. Read anything outside your texts and contacts.
Check the privacy claim yourself
InboxIQ does not have the internet permission, so Android does not let it send anything over Wi-Fi or mobile data. You do not have to take our word for it:
Turn on airplane mode. Reading, searching and sorting work exactly the same.
In Android Settings, open the data usage list. InboxIQ should show no data used.
The code is public at github.com/tsushanth/InboxIQ. The app manifest has no INTERNET entry.
With a computer and USB debugging: adb shell dumpsys package com.inboxiq.app | grep INTERNET prints nothing.
One optional exception: if you choose the larger sorting model in Settings, Google Play downloads it. InboxIQ itself still opens no connection.
Next, Android shows its own confirmation screen. Nothing changes until you confirm there.
Choose InboxIQ as default SMS app
Android did not switch your default SMS app, so nothing changed. You can try again whenever you like.

Things to try
Open the Codes tab. A one-time code shows a Copy code button for a few minutes.
Open Junk to see what was filed as spam or scam. If one is wrong, open it and change its label.
Swipe a conversation right to archive it, or select it to pin or mute it.
Got it
Notifications are off
While InboxIQ is your default SMS app, new texts only alert you if notifications are on. Without them you would miss messages.
Turn on notifications
Open notification settings
No transactions
Bank and payment alerts, bills, orders, deliveries, tickets and appointments show up here, kept apart from your conversations.

Transactions are automated alerts about money, orders, deliveries and bookings. They get their own tab and a notification channel with sound but no pop-up. Conversations you filed by hand are never moved.
